demographics.overall_disability_percentage: 2.21% (Census 2011, NSS, LASI), representing over 26.8 million citizens
demographics.visual_impairment_seeing: 18.8% of disabled population (~0.42% of total population). In adults 45+, LASI indicates 33.8% suffer from distance vision impairment and 43% near-vision impairment.
demographics.hearing_impairment: 18.9% of disabled population (~0.42% national share). WHO clinical estimates place significant hearing loss higher at roughly 6.3%. In seniors 65+, 1 in 3 (33.3%) experience presbycusis.
demographics.speech_impairment_mute: 7.5% of disabled population (~0.16% of total population). Prevalent in early childhood (ages 5-14) during language acquisition.

top_states_by_disability_burden.key_challenges: Highest raw population burden; low rural household incomes make digital screen readers and refreshable Braille unaffordable; dependency on basic mechanical slates.
Large working-age adult population; urban centers have tech access while rural regions like Vidarbha and Marathwada face deep gaps.
Steep multidimensional poverty clusters; ₹20,000+ digital hearing aids and ₹12,00,000 cochlear implants are out of reach without philanthropy.
High rural concentration; severe shortage of Telugu-first accessible screen reading tools.
High age-related sensory decline (cataracts and presbycusis); urgent need for Bengali audio and tactile resources.

demographics.unmet_technology_need: 70% to 71% of people with disabilities in India lack access to necessary assistive hardware and software (WHO-UNICEF GReAT report).
demographics.out_of_pocket_crisis: 67.4% of all assistive technology items acquired in India must be paid for completely out-of-pocket by low-income families.
demographics.rural_divide: 68% of India's disabled population resides in rural areas with minimal tech training centers or repair infrastructure.
